column1: # Corpus B — third-party trees, pinned to a commit.
# Pinned because this is the only corpus whose per-rule counts may gate: a count
# is a property of the tree, so it is reproducible only against a fixed one.
# Bumping a sha is a deliberate re-baselining commit, which is the review moment
# where a change in the numbers gets looked at.
# Fetched at depth 1 — poly reads no git history, so depth is pure cost.
# Licences are all permissive (MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / ISC / Unlicense); the
# orchestrator refuses anything else, because a CI artifact derived from a copyleft
# tree is a redistribution question we have no reason to take on.
# Every row below is pinned to a commit (resolved 2026-08-31). A newly added row
# may carry a branch name for one commit: `harden.sh` records `pinned: false` for
# a non-sha ref and refuses to gate per-rule counts on that root, because a count
# measured against a moving branch is not reproducible and a gate built on one
# fires on somebody else's merge. Resolve with `git ls-remote <url> <branch>` and
# commit the sha before relying on its numbers.
